question: By what means, described as mere knowledge and as what has been heard, is a result said to be attained in addressing one of fair face?
premises: An instrument is indicated by this.
That instrument is characterized as mere knowledge.
It is also characterized as what has been heard.
The address is to one of fair face.
inference: By this, by mere knowledge and by what has been heard, something is attained, O one of fair face.
uncertainties: Result attained is not stated within the verse
plain_english: By this, by mere knowledge and by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.
